Read out of saint.gr's line for 13 Αυγούστου, «Άγιος Τύχων Επίσκοπος Ζαντόνσκ», with the rank word and the see left off. The page glosses the name from τύχη, the fortunate, the auspicious, and gives his name in the world as Τιμόθεος Σοκολώφ.

death.note: As printed by days.pravoslavie.ru: “Преставление (1783), второе обретение мощей (1991) свт. Тихона, еп. Воронежского, Задонского чудотворца”.

birth.note: Born in 1724, as the entry’s own life says (azbyka.ru, days.pravoslavie.ru, pravoslavno.rs); recorded 2026-09-06.

attestations.note: The Romanian life behind that line is this man — born 1724 in a poor sacristan's family at Korotsk in the Novgorod diocese, teacher of rhetoric, tonsured Tihon in 1758, bishop of Voronezh in 1761 at thirty-seven, dead at fifty-nine — so this is a row on this folder and not a second Tikhon. Read 24 September 2026.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 13ης Αυγούστου — «Άγιος Τύχων Επίσκοπος Ζαντόνσκ»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 13 Αυγούστου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. The Russian, Romanian and Serbian rows already keep him on this menologion day and the Greek calendar keeps him on the revised-julian 13 August. The head line «Αγιος Τυχων Επισκοπος Ζαντονσκ (1724 - 1783)» agrees with the folder's dates exactly, and the long Greek notice is the same man: Timothy Sokolov, born 1724 at Korotsk in the province of Novgorod, the seminary, teacher of Greek and then of rhetoric from July 1754, tonsured Tikhon on 10 April 1758, teacher of philosophy from 27 August 1758, inspector of the seminary 13 January 1759, Tver from 26 August 1759, consecrated 13 May 1761 at Saint Petersburg as chorbishop of the diocese of Novgorod at thirty-seven. **Two readings of the page differ from what the folder already says and neither is changed here: saint.gr makes his father a deacon, «στην οικογένεια του διακόνου Σαβελλίου», where the folder's Romanian row has a poor sacristan's family; and saint.gr dates his accession to Voronezh to 3 February 1763, «όπου υπηρέτησε 4 χρόνια και 7 μήνες», where the folder's Romanian row has 1761. Both are named in the reader's report.** The page adds a relic: «Απότμημα αφθάρτου Λειψάνου του Αγίου βρίσκεται στη Μονή Παντελεήμονος Αγίου Όρους». No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on the life page. It prints apophthegms and prayers of his at length but no apolytikion and no kontakion, so no hymn is added.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 26.08.2026 (13. август ст. ст.) — „Св. Тихон Задонски, или Воронежски.“

track.note: Born here in 1724; sent to the diocesan school at thirteen, which is the 1737.
The archbishop's school, then the seminary from 1740, kept on to teach from 1754, tonsured and made prefect in 1758.
Archimandrite of the Zheltikov monastery and rector of the seminary. The lots for his consecration were drawn at Petersburg at Pascha 1761 — a visit, not a stay, and not drawn.
Bishop of Keksholm and Ladoga, vicar of Novgorod, from 13 May 1761.
The see, "four and a half years"; given up for his health in 1767.
The Tolshevo monastery in the forest north-east of Voronezh, his first retreat.
The monastery of the Mother of God, from 1769 to his death in 1783; his relics lie here.
